subject: System Design
title: CAP Theorem Deep Dive
description: A quick, practical guide to CAP Theorem Deep Dive.

hook.text: You can have Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance — but never all three at once.

buildup.text: Eric Brewer proposed the CAP theorem in 2000. It became the most debated principle in distributed systems.

discovery.text: During a network partition, you must choose: reject requests (CP) or serve possibly stale data (AP).

twist.text: When there's no partition, you can have both consistency and availability. CAP only kicks in during failures.

climax.text: CAP is a simplification. The real trade-off is a spectrum between consistency and latency in normal operation.

punchline.text: CAP forces a choice only when the network splits.

quiz.question: When does the CAP theorem force a trade-off?
